User is building a Python data pipeline package (modules: processor.py, s3.py, hdfs.py, gpfs.py, encryption.py, compression.py, checksum.py, exceptions.py) that downloads data from HDFS/GPFS, optionally encrypts, zips, checksums, uploads to S3, and archives. #data-pipeline #python

The package's exceptions.py defines custom exceptions: S3OperationException, HdfsOperationException, GpfsOperationException, EncryptionException, CompressionException, ChecksumException. #data-pipeline #exceptions

s3.py defines S3Uploader and S3Downloader classes, each taking bucket_name in __init__ and creating a boto3 client. upload_directory/download_directory walk a directory, build s3_key as basename(directory)/relative_path, and attach a "checksum" value in S3 object Metadata. #data-pipeline #s3

Both S3Uploader and S3Downloader in s3.py have a _get_checksum(relative_path, checksum_file_path) helper that reads a CSV of "relative_path,checksum" lines and returns the matching checksum (or ""). Checksums are stored in checksums.csv. #data-pipeline #s3

Processor.__init__(process_name, operation, data_source_type, data_source_path, encryption_needed, zipping_needed, checksum_needed, s3_upload, archive_needed, process_sub_folder_path="", s3_path="") in processor.py drives the pipeline via a run() method. #data-pipeline #processor

Processor.run() creates a working directory at os.path.abspath(process_name), downloads from HDFS or GPFS when operation=="download", raises ValueError for an invalid data_source_type, then encrypts, zips, generates/writes checksums.csv, uploads to S3, and optionally archives with shutil.make_archive. #data-pipeline #processor

When s3_upload is enabled during a download operation, Processor.run() uses S3Downloader to pull files into process_sub_folder_path and compares checksums.csv against locally generated checksums, raising S3OperationException on mismatch or missing checksum file. #data-pipeline #processor
